elements.html:
What is the purpose of the research?

The research is organized by Beatriz Sousa, Undergraduate Student at the School of Psychology at Bournemouth University as part of the Psychology Project Unit.  As a dissertation project, this work is supervised by Dr Ellen Seiss.

 

This study aims to investigate how emotional stimuli (negative, neutral, and positive) can influence episodic memory performance. Emotions has the ability to enhance or impair our encoding stage and our recalling of information from events. Alexithymia prevents individuals from identifying and processing emotions, including this variable allows us to study the correlation between episodic memory performance and the effects of emotions and alexithymia.

 

During this online study, we will ask you to complete an online survey about initial information (age, gender, etc) before beginning the memory experiment. You will then be provided with an image followed by a short clip; you will then be asked to complete a statement and response item questionnaire about the video you watched. Finally, an alexithymia questionnaire and a scale measuring your self-rating of the valence and arousal you felt towards the initial picture. The study will take 30 minutes to complete.

 

Why have I been invited?

We are looking to recruit 40 female BU psychology undergraduate students. You have been invited because you are 18 to 25 years old, and English is your first language (the language that was the primary language of your birth home and it is the language you are most proficient with) and have normal to corrected to normal vision. Please note that you will not be able to take part in this study if you have any of the exclusion criteria: colour deficiencies in eyesight, learning disability e.g. dyslexia, history of neuropsychiatric disorders that involves prescribed medication of antidepressants/mood suppressors.

 

If the above description does not apply to you, then, please withdraw from the experiment now by closing your browser page, as unfortunately, you are not eligible for this study.

 

Do I have to take part?

It is up to you to decide whether to take part. If you do decide to take part, you will have access to this information sheet to read. We want you to understand what participation involves before you decide on whether to participate. 

 

If you or any family member have an on-going relationship with BU or the research team, e.g. as a member of staff, as student or other service user, your decision on whether to take part (or continue to take part) will not affect this relationship and/or your studies at BU in any way.

 

You can withdraw from participation at any time and without giving a reason, simply by closing the browser page. However, if you choose to withdraw from the experiment before it is finished, you will not be compensated for your time. Please note that due to limited credits available for this study, we require participants to complete the study to the best of their abilities (meaning not skipping the initial stimuli, watching the video, and answering any questions), reaction time to stimuli will be reviewed before granting SONA credits, this is to protect the validity of our study and ensure we are receiving accurate data.

Please note that once you have completed the experiment, we are unable to remove your anonymised responses from the study.

 

How long will the experiment take to complete?

We anticipate that the experiment will take 30 minutes to complete. If you are a BU Psychology student, you will be compensated with 0.5 SONA credits for your time. Unfortunately, we cannot compensate non-Psychology BU students and members of the wider community.

 

What are the advantages and possible disadvantages or risks of taking part?

Whilst there are no immediate benefits for those people participating in the project, this study may advance cognitive understanding of how emotions influence episodic memory and clarify how alexithymia may create barriers, highlighting importance of more effective approaches towards emotional and memory difficulties. 

 

Whilst we do not anticipate any risks to you in taking part in this study, you may feel some discomfort or distress towards stimuli images. Please only take part if you have taken this account. We will provide some relaxing pictures at the end of the study and you are welcome to contact researchers if you have any further concerns. There are also support resources below if you find you need to contact any health professionals.

 

BU students can access support via the University’s Health and Wellbeing Resources page: Health & wellbeing | Bournemouth University

As an alternative, here are the contact details for the Samaritans: t: 116 123, e: jo@samarians.org. 

 

 

 

 

What type of information will be sought from me and why is the collection of this information relevant for achieving the research project’s objectives?

 

We will be collecting initial information about your gender, age, English literacy, eyesight, and medical background stated above, all of which may impact whether you continue with the study. If you meet the criteria, you will be shown an image to stimulate an emotion (positive, negative, or neutral) and reaction time to this stimulus will be considered to ensure the viability of your data. You will then be shown a short video followed by an item statement and response question with the following potential answers: 1) true, 2) false and 3) I do not know. Finally, you will complete an alexithymia questionnaire as well as being presented with the initial image stimuli and a Likert scale (1-9) rating the valence and arousal of the image. The data collected will enable me to establish a correlational relationship between alexithymia levels, emotional stimuli, and episodic memory performance. All data will be anonymised, stored securely and only accessible to the research team.

 

Use of my information

Participation in this study is based on consent: you do not have to complete the survey, and you can change your mind at any point before submitting the survey responses. We will use your data on the basis that it is necessary for the conduct of research, which is an activity in the public interest. We put safeguards in place to ensure that your responses are kept secure and only used as necessary for this research study and associated activities such as a research audit.  

 

You can withdraw from participation at any point by closing your browser window. Once you have submitted your survey response it will not be possible for us to remove it from the study analysis because you will not be identifiable.

 

The anonymous information collected may be used to support other research projects in the future and access to it in this form will not be restricted.  It will not be possible for you to be identified from this data. 

 

Sharing and further use of your personal information

We will share your personal information only with BU staff and the BU student(s) working on the research project.

 

Research results will be included in a final year Psychology Dissertation that will not be made freely available.

 

While anonymity is prioritized, the research team is committed to maintaining a respectful environment in line with research ethical guidelines and thus participants are also expected to engage in this study responsibly. Instances of misuse, harassment, or inappropriate behaviour may exceptionally lead to revoking participants’ anonymity in order to uphold the integrity of the research process.

 

 

Contact for further information

If you have any questions or would like further information, please contact Researcher Beatriz Sousa (email address: s5414180@bournemouth.ac.uk), or Supervisor Dr. Ellen Seiss (email address: eseiss@bournemouth.ac.uk).

 

 

In case of complaints

Any concerns about the study should be directed to Supervisor Dr. Ellen Seiss, (email address: eseiss@bournemouth.ac.uk). If your concerns have not been answered by Supervisor Dr. Ellen Seiss, you should contact Professor Scott Wright, Associate Dean for Research, Innovation and Enterprise in the Faculty of Media, Science and Technology, Bournemouth University by email to researchgovernance@bournemouth.ac.uk.

pages.title: Vividness of Visual Imagery Questionnaire, Marks (1973)
pages.description:
Please complete the VVIQ before moving on to your task.  
This is a 16 item self-report measure of the clarity and liveliness of visual imagery.  
The rating scale is five-point, 5 = perfectly clear and 1 = no image at all, only thinking of object.

rows.text: The exact contours of face, head, shoulders and body.
Characteristic poses of head and attitudes of the body.
The precise carriage, length of step (e.g. in walking).
The different colours of some familiar clothes.

columns.text: Perfectly clear and as vivid as normal vision.
No image at all, you only "know" that you are thinking of an object.

elements.html:
Instructions: Episodic Memory Task 

 The study will begin with emotional memory task. The whole experiment should take 30 minutes of your time.  

 

Before starting, we would like to remind you about our experiment rules.  

 

  1. Please use a desktop or laptop for the task. iPhones and tablets will not work.  

  1. Please make sure you are in a quiet environment where you will not be distracted or disturbed.  

  1. Please switch off any other applications on the computer. These applications will put some pressure on your processor speed which can lead to inaccurate recordings of your performance during the task.  

  1. This task will require your attention for the next 30 minutes. Please ensure that you have the time do this task before proceeding further.  

 

When you are ready to begin – press the link below and it will open a new tab.
